text: your vehicle # What is a vehicle modification Listen Print this page Save page as PDF ### On this page: - What a vehicle modification is - What a vehicle modification is for - How vehicle modifications work - Our Guideline On this page: 1 - What a vehicle modification is 2 - What a vehicle modification is for 3 - How vehicle modifications work 4 - Our Guideline ## What a vehicle modification is You may need changes made to a vehicle so you can drive it or travel in it. We call these changes vehicle modifications. Vehicle modifications can be changes to a car or other type of vehicle you or your family use for your transport. Modifications make sure you can drive the vehicle or be a passenger in the vehicle. Some common modifications include: - wheelchair passenger ramps and wheelchair hoists - modified driving controls - modified restraints and modified car seats. ## What a vehicle modification is for ### Modifications funded because of your disability

In addition to funding modifications to your vehicle, you may also be able to have NDIS funding in your plan for: - assessing your need for a vehicle modification - extra insurance costs because of your modified vehicle - maintenance or repairs of your vehicle modification - help with transport while your vehicle is modified. ### Vehicle ownership You or your family need to own a vehicle that is suitable to modify or have found a suitable vehicle you plan to purchase or lease. You should get advice from an occupational therapist with experience in vehicle modifications if you’re going to purchase a vehicle to modify. This’ll make sure you buy the right type of vehicle that can be modified for your needs. You need permission from the vehicle owner to modify their vehicle and be able to use it most of the time if you don’t own the vehicle. ### Specialised driver training may also be funded We may also fund a specialised vehicle driving instructor for extra lessons you might need: - because of your disability - to learn how to use the modifications in your vehicle. ### What we don’t fund Our rules say what we can fund. We consider your request for vehicle modification funding if it’s: - a support NDIS funds - related to your disability - going to help you work towards your goals - effective and beneficial for you - value for money - legal and safe. We review your vehicle modifications together with all your transport needs to decide the best funded supports for your circumstances. text: modifications ## Step 1: Get advice from an occupational therapist We may fund modifications to a vehicle so you can drive it or travel in it. When considering if we will fund a vehicle modification, we look at if the vehicle modifications and driving supports: - are needed because of your disability - will help you work towards your goals - are NDIS supports . An occupational therapist can give you advice about vehicle modifications. Tip: We can’t fund the purchase of a vehicle It’s important to know we can’t fund the purchase of a vehicle to modify. ## Step 2: Gather your evidence for your planning meeting #### For drivers: get a report from your doctor Your doctor must check you’re fit to drive using the national Assessing Fitness to Drive medical standards if you’re planning to drive a modified vehicle. Download the vehicle modification assessment template: - Vehicle modification assessment template (DOCX 92KB) #### If you’re a passenger We need an assessment from an occupational therapist to understand what changes are needed to your vehicle to travel in it safely if you’re not driving. We’ll also need to know if you: - own the vehicle - plan to buy or lease the vehicle. The first is a hook format and the second is a shorter format without a hook. The third format will be what is used by residents in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. This permit has a plastic pocket into which the existing NSW Mobility Parking Scheme photo permit or the existing ACT Mobility Parking Scheme permit must be inserted. If a valid NSW or ACT permit is not inserted in the plastic pocket, the words 'Void if no NSW (or ACT) permit inserted here' will be visible. In some states, territories and local government areas, separate parking permits may continue to be provided for specific purposes. These permits are not part of the Australian Disability Parking Scheme. Some organisations that transport eligible people with disability may receive an Australian Disability Parking Permit. Permits must only be used when the vehicle is being used to transport the permit holder. Permits must be clearly displayed so the permit number and expiry date are visible from the exterior of the vehicle. Hook permits must be removed from display before the vehicle is driven. This is to ensure the permit does not obscure the vision of the driver. Remember that all Australian Disability Parking Permit holders should check the local rules for parking and obey all other road and parking conditions. Information about these rules and where to apply for an Australian Disability Parking Permit can be obtained through existing state, territory and local government agencies. text: Assessing Fitness to Drive The Standards apply in every Australian state and territory and are used when making licensing decisions for private and commercial drivers of heavy vehicles, light vehicles and motorcycles. They support nationally consistent, evidence-based decisions that balance road safety with personal mobility. Health professionals use the Standards to assess a patient's medical fitness to drive and provide recommendations to driver licensing authorities. The Standards include advice on how medical conditions may impact a person’s ability to drive safely and are informed by the latest medical evidence and input from: - medical associations - patient representative groups - driver licensing authorities - industry. We review the medical standards approximately every three years. The review of the 2022 Edition of the Assessing Fitness to Drive Standards has now begun . text: changes from the previous edition (2016) and the current edition. ## The NTC and Austroads The AFTD Standards are a joint publication of the National Transport Commission (NTC) and Austroads. The NTC leads the development and review of the medical content in consultation with health professionals, clinical experts, driver licensing authorities, industry, consumer groups and road safety researchers. Austroads publishes the Standards and supports their implementation by organisations that use them. The Standards are approved by Commonwealth, state and territory transport ministers through the Infrastructure and Transport Ministers' Meeting. ## Where does the Standards apply The Standards are used by driver licensing authorities in every Australian state and territory when considering medical fitness to drive for: - heavy vehicles - light vehicles - motorcycles. text: ## How to get modifications made ### Talk to an Occupational Therapist Before having a vehicle modified, we recommend you book an appointment with a suitably qualified occupational therapist. Occupational therapists can organise on-and-off-road training and driving assessments . They can recommend vehicle modifications and equipment suitable for your specific needs. See Driving assessments for more information. Find an occupational therapist ### Find a qualified modifier The certifier ensures all modifications are assessed and found to be compliant and safe for use in road transport. Back to top ## Who can receive it You may be eligible for MVCS if you: - are impaired because of an accepted injury or condition - are clinically assessed as: - unable to drive safely in a vehicle without driving or other modifications; or - unable to be driven safely in a vehicle without modifications The eligibility criteria and conditions under which funding may be considered are set out in the Motor Vehicle Compensation Scheme Legislative Instrument. ## What you can receive If you're eligible, we may be able to pay a subsidy towards or the total cost of: - driving or other clinically required modifications to a vehicle you already own; or - driving or other clinically required modifications to a vehicle you purchase at your own cost; or - a vehicle with driving or other clinically

source_title: Fitness to drive and medical conditions
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: Fitness to drive and medical conditions Category: fitness_to_drive Publisher: National Transport Commission / Austroads / state transport authorities URL: https://www.ntc.gov.au/codes-and-guidelines/assessing-fitness-to-drive Description: National medical standards and state licensing context for people whose disability or medical condition may affect safe driving, including conditional licences, practical assessments and vehicle modifications. Care team notes: Do not tell someone whether they personally can drive. Advise discussing changes with their doctor and state/territory licensing authority, especially with progressive weakness, fatigue, medications or cognitive change.

source_title: NDIS vehicle modifications
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: NDIS vehicle modifications Category: vehicle_modifications_ndis Publisher: NDIS URL: https://www.ndis.gov.au/participants/assistive-technology/modifying-your-vehicle/how-get-vehicle-modified Description: NDIS information on vehicle modifications for driving or travelling as a passenger, evidence requirements, doctor reports, driver-trained OT assessments, quotes, repairs and limits on what NDIS does not fund. Care team notes: Be clear that NDIS may fund disability-related modifications but not purchase, registration, ordinary running costs or general driving lessons.

source_title: Driver-trained occupational therapy assessment
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: Driver-trained occupational therapy assessment Category: driving_assessment Publisher: NDIS / DVA / NSW Government URL: https://www.ndis.gov.au/participants/assistive-technology/modifying-your-vehicle/how-get-vehicle-modified Description: Information on when driver-trained OT assessment may be needed for modified driving controls, vehicle-specific disability driving tests, safety certification and training in using vehicle modifications. Care team notes: For MND, link this with occupational therapy, physiotherapy, fatigue, weakness, reaction time, respiratory equipment and communication needs.

source_title: Australian disability parking permits
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: Australian disability parking permits Category: parking_permits Publisher: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing / myGov URL: https://www.health.gov.au/our-work/australian-disability-parking-scheme?language=en Description: National disability parking scheme information and state/territory application pathways for mobility parking permits and concessions. Care team notes: Tell users to check their state/territory authority for eligibility, application, cost and local parking rules. Permits must only be used when transporting the permit holder.

source_title: Patient travel assistance schemes
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: Patient travel assistance schemes Category: patient_travel_subsidy Publisher: myGov / state and territory health services URL: https://my.gov.au/en/services/health-and-disability/living-with-disability/discounts-and-subsidies-in-your-state-if-you-have-disability Description: State and territory patient travel subsidy pathways for people who need to travel long distances for medical treatment, including travel and accommodation support links. Care team notes: Ask the user's state/territory and appointment location before answering. These schemes differ by jurisdiction and usually need forms/referrals/receipts.

source_title: Community transport and accessible transport
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: Community transport and accessible transport Category: community_accessible_transport Publisher: Disability Gateway / myGov URL: https://www.disabilitygateway.gov.au/transport/driving Description: Disability Gateway and myGov transport guidance, including community transport, accessible parking, state/territory resources and transport subsidies. Care team notes: For practical answers, combine this with the person's MND association, local council, NDIS transport funding, My Aged Care transport support and carer availability.

source_title: State modified vehicle rules
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: State modified vehicle rules Category: state_vehicle_rules Publisher: NSW Government / Queensland Government URL: https://www.nsw.gov.au/driving-boating-and-transport/driver-and-rider-licences/health-conditions-and-disability/driving-or-riding-disability/modified-vehicles Description: State examples for modified vehicles, licence conditions, certification, medical certificates and when a vehicle-specific driving test or modified-vehicle condition may apply. Care team notes: Use state examples carefully. Ask location and refer to that state/territory authority because licence and vehicle certification processes differ.

source_title: DVA vehicle modification support
text: Driving, transport, travel and vehicle modification record: DVA vehicle modification support Category: veterans_vehicle_support Publisher: Department of Veterans' Affairs URL: https://www.dva.gov.au/what-we-help-with/vehicle-costs-and-benefits/motor-vehicle-compensation-scheme Description: DVA vehicle modification and driving assessment information for eligible veterans with accepted service-related injuries or illnesses that limit mobility. Care team notes: Only suggest this pathway if the user may be DVA-entitled. It is separate from NDIS and state transport schemes.
